## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

```{r 13C/18O}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(data, aes(x = `δ18O in ‰ vs DeltaSMOW`, 
                 y = `δ13C (‰ v.s.V-PDB)`,colour = Sub)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ name, ncol = 3) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = expression(delta^{18}*O),
    y = expression(delta^{13}*C),
    title = "Relationship between δ13C and δ18O per species"
  )


```
```{r histograms}

species_vector <- c(
  "Pouteria torta",
  "Alchornea lojaensis",
  "Weinmania  loxensis",
  "Clarisia  racemosa",
  "Myrcia sp nov",
  "Hedyosmun  purpurascens"
) 
plot_6_species_histograms <- function(data, species_vector, var_name = "iWUE") {
  
  # set grid: 2 rows × 3 columns
  par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
  
  for (sp in species_vector) {
    df <- subset(data, name == sp)
    
    # check if variable exists
    
    x <- df[[var_name]]
    
    # if no data
    if (length(x) == 0 || !is.numeric(x)) {
      plot.new()
      title(main = paste("No data for:", sp))
      next
    }
    
    hist(x,
         main = paste("Histogram:", sp),
         xlab = var_name)
  }
}
plot_6_species_histograms(data, species_vector, var_name = "iWUE (μmol/mol)") #add the different variables here.


```

```{r IGNORAR modelos lineares por especie con N+P}
models  <- list(
  "Pouteria iWUE" = mod_iWUE_pt,
  "Pouteria O18"  = mod_O18_pt,
  "Pouteria N15"  = mod_N15_pt,
  "Pouteria CN"   = mod_CN_pt,

  "Clarisia iWUE" = mod_iWUE_cr,
  "Clarisia O18"  = mod_O18_cr,
  "Clarisia N15"  = mod_N15_cr,
  "Clarisia CN"   = mod_CN_cr,

  "Alchornea iWUE" = mod_iWUE_al,
  "Alchornea O18"  = mod_O18_al,
  "Alchornea N15"  = mod_N15_al,
  "Alchornea CN"   = mod_CN_al,

  "Myrcia iWUE" = mod_iWUE_my,
  "Myrcia O18"  = mod_O18_my,
  "Myrcia N15"  = mod_N15_my,
  "Myrcia CN"   = mod_CN_my,

  "Hedyosmum iWUE" = mod_iWUE_hp,
  "Hedyosmum O18"  = mod_O18_hp,
  "Hedyosmum N15"  = mod_N15_hp,
  "Hedyosmum CN"   = mod_CN_hp,

  "Weinmania iWUE" = mod_iWUE_wl,
  "Weinmania O18"  = mod_O18_wl,
  "Weinmania N15"  = mod_N15_wl,
  "Weinmania CN"   = mod_CN_wl)
# exportar tabla
tab <- modelsummary(
  models,
  output = "data.frame",
  stars = TRUE,
  gof_map = c("nobs", "r2.marginal", "aic")
)

# transponer
tab_t <- as.data.frame(t(tab))

# fijar nombres de columna usando la primera fila
colnames(tab_t) <- tab_t[1, ]
tab_t <- tab_t[-1, ]  # quitar fila original de nombres

# mostrar tabla
kable(tab_t)

```

#### TABLA ANOVA 1000
```{r TABLAS ANOVA 1000 }

mods_1000 <- list(
  "Pouteria iWUE" = anova_model_iWUE,
  "δ18O" = anova_model_18O,
  "δ15N" = anova_model_15N,
  "C:N"  = anova_model_CN,
  "Clarisia iWUE " = anova_model_iWUE_cr,
  "δ18O" = anova_model_18O_cr,
  "δ15N" = anova_model_15N_cr,
  "C:N"  = anova_model_CN_cr
)

modelsummary(
  mods_1000,
  statistic = "({statistic}, p = {p.value})",
  stars = c('*' = .05, '**' = .01, '***' = .001),
  fmt = 2,
  output = "markdown",
  title = "ANOVA results for *1000 species*")
```


Pouteria: 
iWUE relevant NxP
d18O N, P, no the interaction
d15N .
C:N only with P.

Clarisia:
d18I for N,
d15N for N
C:N for N
Clarisia N is important.
